paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, so I'm not going to joke about the hard part. Here's what I see. John told Herod the truth: "It is not lawful for you to have her." (Matthew 14:4) And it cost him. Doing right doesn't always come with a happy ending right away. I think that's one of the hardest things in the whole Bible to sit with.

Now look at Herod. He wanted John dead, but he was afraid of the people. (Matthew 14:5) Later he was grieved, but because of his oaths and his guests, he ordered that her wish be granted. (Matthew 14:9) He felt the right thing and still did the wrong thing, because he cared more about how he looked than about what was true. Friend, I've seen that in a lot of people. Honestly, I've seen it in a stamper or two.

So what do we do with this? We keep telling the truth, even when it's costly, and we don't let fear of a crowd steer us. And notice the end. John's disciples came, buried his body, and went and informed Jesus. (Matthew 14:12) When things fall apart, they took it straight to Jesus. Baker, that's where you can take your hardest days too.
